name: Herod Antipas and Herodias
charge: Taking his brother's wife; beheading John for saying so
summary: Herod the tetrarch married Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, and John told him it was not lawful. Herodias wanted John dead; Herod feared him and heard him gladly, but at his birthday feast swore to give her dancing daughter whatever she asked. She asked for John's head on a charger.
offense: Leviticus twice: thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy brother's wife. Then a rash oath kept at the cost of a prophet's life, for the sake of them which sat with him. Christ called him that fox and would not answer him at his trial.
judgment: Scripture records no sentence on Herod or Herodias; the gospels leave them at Christ's trial, mocking him. History records Antipas exiled by Caligula at his wife's ambition. The record here is the crime and the statute.

entries.commentary: In his own country they are astonished at his wisdom and his mighty works, and then are offended at him because they know his family. A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house. What was done to him is done to those teaching today: men who knew you before you repented ask who you think you are.

He could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk and healed them, and he marvelled because of their unbelief. Consider what that means. The unbelief of his own people was such that it made the son of the Most High marvel.

He sends them forth by two and two with power over unclean spirits, taking nothing for the journey but a staff. Whosoever will not receive you nor hear you, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. The word goes out whether they hear or whether they forbear, and that shaking of the dust seals the judgment.

Herod hears of him and says it is John, whom he beheaded, risen from the dead. John had told Herod plainly, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife. Herod knew the law well enough to be accused by it, because those rulers were schooled in the customs of Israel.

Herodias had a quarrel against John and would have killed him, but could not, for Herod feared him, knowing that he was a just man and an holy. When the oath is made, the daughter asks her mother what to ask, and is told, The head of John the Baptist. The king was exceeding sorry, but for his oath's sake he sent the executioner.

He was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things. Five loaves and two fishes feed five thousand men, and twelve baskets of fragments are taken up. He made them sit down by companies, in ranks by hundreds and by fifties. No man argued about where he was placed. The Most High is a God of order, and the eating came after the order.

He comes to them walking upon the sea, and they suppose it had been a spirit and cry out. These were fishermen; they knew what water does. They were sore amazed, for they considered not the miracle of the loaves, for their heart was hardened. Men can watch a thing done in front of them and still not take it to heart.
Wherever he entered, they laid the sick in the streets and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment, and as many as touched him were made whole.
The rulers of that hour are named, and Annas and Caiaphas are both called high priests. There was to be one, and the naming of two shows how far out of order that priesthood had come.
John preaches the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins, as it is written in the book of the words of Esaias: the voice of one crying in the wilderness.

O generation of vipers, bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father. Being dipped in water without works that go with it is not what is written here. The fruits worthy of repentance are the works.

He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none. The publicans are told to exact no more than that which is appointed them, and the soldiers to do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely, and be content with their wages.

I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh, he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire, and he will gather the wheat into his garner, but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.
Herod, being reproved by him for Herodias his brother Philip's wife, and for all the evils which he had done, added yet this above all, that he shut up John in prison.

Jesus being baptized and praying, the heaven was opened, and the Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove upon him, and a voice came from heaven, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.

Jesus began to be about thirty years of age, being, as was supposed, the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli. Heli was the father of Mary, so this line is reckoned through the son-in-law. The generations run back through Nathan and David, through Judah, Jacob, Isaac and Abraham, through Sem and Noe, and to Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.

Of the Galilaeans whose blood Pilate mingled with their sacrifices, and of the eighteen upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, he says they were not sinners above all others. I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish. It is said twice, in the same words.

Three years he came seeking fruit on the fig tree and found none, and the dresser asks for one more year to dig about it and dung it. If it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down. Three years is the length of his own ministry among the people, and Jerusalem was cut down after it.

A woman bowed together eighteen years and unable to lift herself up is loosed from her infirmity, and immediately made straight. The ruler of the synagogue answers with indignation that there are six days in which men ought to work. Thou hypocrite, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering? Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day? All his adversaries were ashamed, and all the people rejoiced.
The kingdom of God is like a grain of mustard seed which grew and waxed a great tree, and like leaven hid in three measures of meal till the whole was leavened.

Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many will seek to enter in, and shall not be able. The strait way is a narrow one, walked by discipline: correction, falling, getting back up, and correcting yourself. Many hear this word and turn back to the world rather than walk it. We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets. And he shall say, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity. They shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God. They come from the four corners because they were scattered to the four corners.

The Pharisees tell him to depart, for Herod will kill him, and he answers, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow. I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem. He knew his work and would not be moved off it by a threat.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

They accuse him of perverting the nation and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, and Pilate says, I find no fault in this man. Matthew's account gives the reason he could see it: he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

Herod was exceeding glad, hoping to have seen some miracle done by him, and questioned him in many words, but he answered him nothing. He had nothing to say to that house. Its head had sought his life as a child, and this one had beheaded John.

Pilate says a third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him. He knew the man was innocent and gave sentence anyway. Barabbas, cast into prison for sedition and murder, is released, and Jesus is delivered to their will.

Simon a Cyrenian is laid hold upon and made to bear the cross after him. Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children. If they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

Two malefactors, criminals, are led with him to be put to death, and they crucified him at the place called Calvary. Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. The superscription written over him in Greek, Latin and Hebrew reads, This is the King of the Jews.

One malefactor railed on him; the other rebuked him, took the blame of his own deeds, and said, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. That man repented at the last hour, and was answered, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

There was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour, and the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst. The rending of the veil is a sign. What stood between the holy place and the holiest was opened, and the sacrificial service under the first testament was coming to its end.
The centurion glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man, and all the people that came together to that sight smote their breasts and returned.

Joseph of Arimathaea, a good man and a just, had not consented to their counsel and deed, and begged the body and laid it in a sepulchre hewn in stone. He was buried the same day, which is the custom written in the law. There is no waiting days over a body. The women returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment. That is written after the death, in the new testament.

In Egypt the children of Israel served the gods of Egypt, dressed like Egyptians, and were fully engulfed in the Egyptian way of life; Moses himself was raised as an Egyptian in the house of Pharaoh. The Most High told them to leave all of that back in Egypt. The same word stands for us: when the Most High redeems us out of this captivity, many of the customs we learned here will be cut off, because they are not coming into the kingdom. The land of Canaan was full of idols. If Israel obeyed His voice the Most High would be an enemy to their enemies, bless their bread and water, and take sickness away; the charge in Canaan was not to bow to their gods nor do after their works, but to utterly overthrow them and break down their images. Coming out of Egypt required a transformed mind: not conformed to the way of life of Egypt or Canaan, but renewed to the commandments of the Most High.

Keep the statutes and judgments of the Most High, which if a man do, he shall live in them. The Ten Commandments are not the whole of the law but a summary. Under the Sabbath commandment sit sub-statutes such as no buying, no selling, no working; likewise under the law of adultery sit all the laws of this chapter, the ordinances of marriage and the forbidden beds. None of you shall approach to any that is near of kin to uncover their nakedness; these laws name who a man may not lay down with.

The nakedness of thy father's wife is thy father's nakedness; that is the stepmother. The wicked mind reasons that she is not the biological mother, so it is fine to lust after her; the scripture says no, that is wicked. This very sin was reported among the Corinthians, a fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife. The law had already forbidden it, and it was being done in Egypt and Canaan; that is why the Most High opened the chapter the way He did.

The sister, whether born at home or born abroad, and the son's daughter and the daughter's daughter are all forbidden; the grandchildren's nakedness is thine own nakedness. There are sick spirits out there, and some of them are grandfathers, uncles, and fathers. Be careful and mindful who you leave your children around; do not hand your children to just anybody for the sake of your own pleasure.

The father's sister, the mother's sister, and the wife of the father's brother, thine aunt, are all near kinswomen and off limits. Incest is still practiced among the nations of this land, and children born of incestuous unions often carry defects and disabilities; the law guards the seed.

The daughter in law, the brother's wife, and a woman with her daughter or her granddaughter are all forbidden; it is wickedness. Neither take a wife to her sister to vex her, to uncover her nakedness beside the other in her lifetime; that also shuts down what the world today calls threesomes.

A woman put apart for her uncleanness is a woman in her menstrual cycle. A man must wait the appointed seven days, and if the issue runs beyond, wait again; [Leviticus 15](/bible/leviticus/15) details these laws of uncleanness, taught in the previous class.
To lie carnally with thy neighbour's wife is adultery. This world even sings songs celebrating adultery; the law forbids defiling thyself with her.

Passing seed through the fire to Molech was child sacrifice: the nations slew their newborn children and offered them to that god, and Israel learned it from them, as Ezekiel testifies of Jerusalem slaying the children of the Most High. The abortions of today are no different. The Most High is bringing spirits into the earth, and the child is slain so the parents can go on living as they please; that is the same sacrifice unto Molech, and it is wickedness.

Abomination means a thing that causes disgust or hatred. When a man lies with mankind as with womankind, the Most High calls it disgusting and hateful. What a man hates and finds disgusting he removes far from himself; so we must teach our people to repent and come out of the things the Most High hates.
Lying with any beast is confusion, for man and for woman alike. The nations have set up places where these strange lusts are fulfilled, and the sin is found among every people; it is all wickedness.

In all these things the nations were defiled which the Most High cast out; the Egyptians and the Canaanites were doing these very abominations, and the land itself was defiled by them. The land spews out the defiled. That is why Israel was put out of Jerusalem: we could not abide in the land with our sins, sacrificing to idol gods and working all manner of evil, so the Most High raised up an enemy to carry us into bondage and remove us out of the land. Whosoever commits any of these abominations, the souls that commit them shall be cut off from among their people, meaning put to death.

Whosoever of Israel or of the strangers in the land gave of his seed unto Molech was surely put to death; the people of the land stoned him with stones. This is the child sacrifice shown in [Ezekiel 16](/bible/ezekiel/16), slaying the children of the Most High and delivering them to pass through the fire. If the people of the land hid their eyes from the man and killed him not, the Most High set His face against that man and against his family. When you see wickedness you must utter it and expose it; a witness that holds his peace bears iniquity. Sin brings judgment on a whole house. Achan coveted the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver, and the wedge of gold, and he and his sons and his daughters and all that he had were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family.

The soul that turns after such as have familiar spirits and after wizards, to go a whoring after them, is cut off from among his people. Sanctify yourselves and be ye holy; keep the statutes of the Most High, for He is the Lord which sanctifieth you. Every one that curseth his father or his mother shall surely be put to death; his blood shall be upon him. Disrespecting your mother and your father carried the death penalty.

The man that committeth adultery with another man's wife, the adulterer and the adulteress, shall surely be put to death. This world openly defends adultery and men even boast of committing it with another man's wife; the scriptures call for death upon both.

The man that lies with his father's wife, and the man that lies with his daughter in law, shall surely be put to death; they have wrought confusion. If a man lie with mankind as he lieth with a woman, both have committed an abomination and shall surely be put to death; abomination means hateful and disgusting unto the Most High. The man that takes a wife and her mother is burnt with fire, both he and they, that there be no wickedness among you. The man or woman that lies with a beast is put to death, and the beast is slain also. All of these judgments fall under the laws of adultery, the sub-statutes of that commandment.

The man that takes his sister and sees her nakedness, it is a wicked thing; they are cut off in the sight of their people, and he bears his iniquity. The man that lies with a woman having her sickness, her menstrual cycle, has discovered her fountain, and both are cut off from among their people; this goes with the laws of [Leviticus 15](/bible/leviticus/15). The nakedness of the mother's sister and the father's sister is near kin; they bear their iniquity. He that lies with his uncle's wife or takes his brother's wife, they shall die childless.

Keep all my statutes and all my judgments, that the land whither I bring you spew you not out. Walk not in the manners of the nation cast out before you, for they committed all these things and therefore the Most High abhorred them. I am the Lord your God, which have separated you from other people. The Most High separated Israel from the other people, so Israel is to walk differently; these laws are the separation.

Put difference between clean beasts and unclean, and between unclean fowls and clean; this goes back to [Leviticus 11](/bible/leviticus/11), the dietary laws. No shrimp, crab, lobster, pork, catfish, and the like; everything is not clean, whatever the church teaches. If you eat whatever you please, you are not separating yourself from the other nations. Ye shall be holy unto me, for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.

A man or woman that hath a familiar spirit, or that is a wizard, was surely put to death by stoning. The tarot card readings, the fortune telling, and the horoscopes of today are that same dealing with familiar spirits; do not touch any of it.

verses.text: For Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife: for he had married her.
For John had said unto Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother’s wife.
Therefore Herodias had a quarrel against him, and would have killed him; but she could not:
For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just man and an holy, and observed him; and when he heard him, he did many things, and heard him gladly.
And when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief estates of Galilee;
And when the daughter of the said Herodias came in, and danced, and pleased Herod and them that sat with him, the king said unto the damsel, Ask of me whatsoever thou wilt, and I will give it thee.
And he sware unto her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me, I will give it thee, unto the half of my kingdom.
And she went forth, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptist.
And she came in straightway with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou give me by and by in a charger the head of John the Baptist.
And the king was exceeding sorry; yet for his oath’s sake, and for their sakes which sat with him, he would not reject her.
And immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison,
And brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother.
For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife.
For John said unto him, It is not lawful for thee to have her.
And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.
But when Herod’s birthday was kept, the daughter of Herodias danced before them, and pleased Herod.
Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatsoever she would ask.
And she, being before instructed of her mother, said, Give me here John Baptist’s head in a charger.
And the king was sorry: nevertheless for the oath’s sake, and them which sat with him at meat, he commanded it to be given her.
And he sent, and beheaded John in the prison.
And his head was brought in a charger, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother.
But Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him for Herodias his brother Philip’s wife, and for all the evils which Herod had done,
Added yet this above all, that he shut up John in prison.
The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying unto him, Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee.
And he said unto them, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.
And when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceeding glad: for he was desirous to see him of a long season, because he had heard many things of him; and he hoped to have seen some miracle done by him.
Then he questioned with him in many words; but he answered him nothing.
And the chief priests and scribes stood and vehemently accused him.
And Herod with his men of war set him at nought, and mocked him, and arrayed him in a gorgeous robe, and sent him again to Pilate.
And the same day Pilate and Herod were made friends together: for before they were at enmity between themselves.
Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy brother’s wife: it is thy brother’s nakedness.
And if a man shall take his brother’s wife, it is an unclean thing: he hath uncovered his brother’s nakedness; they shall be childless.

lawsResolved.text: Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.

If a person swears thoughtlessly with his lips to do evil or to do good, and whatever he pronounced by the oath is hidden or unknown to him, when he comes to know it, then he shall be guilty in these matters and shall confess them.
We should avoid making any oaths so that you may not fall under judgment.
It is an abomination for a civil ruler to commit wickedness, for his office is established on righteousness.
Killing for hire is condemned (the assassin and the one who hires him are both guilty of murder).
